title: Learning Incompressible 3D Flows from Sparse Samples: A Set Transformer Approach to Divergence-Free Kernel Fitting
abstract: arXiv:2610.16645v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recovering divergence-free velocity fields from sparse and corrupted observations requires reconciling physical consistency, expressive representations, and robustness to missing data. We introduce DFK-Former, a set-to-field transformer that reconstructs divergence-free velocity fields from sparse, noisy, and irregularly sampled 3D observations. The model is inherently invariant to the number and ordering of input samples and predicts the parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation, producing continuous, mesh-free velocity fields that satisfy incompressibility exactly by construction rather than approximately through soft constraints or projection operators. Unlike existing divergence-free kernel approaches, which estimate kernel coefficients via a separate optimization for each field, DFK-Former predicts these coefficients directly in a single forward pass. tldr: 提出DFK-Former，一种集合Transformer模型，可从稀疏、含噪、不规则采样的三维观测中通过单次前向传播直接预测无散度核参数，以构造方式精确满足不可压缩性，快速重建连续且无需网格的速度场。
en_tdlr: DFK-Former is a set-to-field transformer that predicts divergence-free kernel parameters in a single forward pass from sparse, noisy, and irregularly sampled 3D observations, producing continuous mesh-free velocity fields that satisfy incompressibility exactly by construction.
